utterances.text: I just moved to Nashville and look who came to visit me. She said that I'm going to starve to death down here if I don't learn how to cook. So today we're going to learn how to fix cornbread. What's the most important step?
Yeah, you can read, can't you?
Well yeah, I can read, man. Got our egg and our milk. Let's take a big old sip of that egg, girl.

When you break an egg, if it's a farm fresh egg, you always want to break it in a cup because if you don't, it could be bad because hens don't know to get off of them. They think they're their babies. I got some. There's your pro chicken tip there, young man Roberts.
Now, wait a second. I saw this chef online say that the secret to the best Nashville cornbread is a big spoonful of white sugar in the batter. Let's get that in there.
Put that spoon down. We are not making cake, we are making cornbread. If you put sugar in that bowl, I am walking out of this kitchen right now and you can starve in peace.
But Grandma, it balances the salt! It's the new way of doing it for the vlog.

I don't care about a 'vlog.' I care about your soul. We are going to sit here and stare at this batter until you realize that sugar has no business in a skillet. I'm waiting. You want to cook, or you want to play?
All right, I got my batter in here. Now I'm going to put some pepper in here. What do you think? How do you think it's going to taste, man?
Mm, good. Okay. Mm, here, try that.
Oh, oh, that's good. I don't think I'm going to be starving now.
